headword: {不祝儀袋|ふしゅうぎぶくろ}
gloss: condolence money envelope; funeral gift envelope

definitions.gloss: condolence money envelope; funeral gift envelope
definitions.explanation: A special envelope used to present money at funerals and other solemn occasions. Tied with black-and-white or silver cords and marked with somber labels, in contrast to the festive envelopes used for weddings.

examples.japanese: {不祝儀袋|ふしゅうぎぶくろ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{用意|ようい}する→用意する：22428_youisuru⟧。
examples.english: I'll prepare a condolence money envelope.

examples.english: You write your name on a condolence envelope with pale ink.

examples.english: Unlike the ones for weddings, condolence envelopes use black-and-white decorative cords.

notes:
Formed from {不祝儀|ふしゅうぎ} (an inauspicious occasion such as a funeral) + {袋|ぶくろ} (bag, envelope). Used at funerals, memorial services, and other solemn events.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {不祝儀袋|ふしゅうぎぶくろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{包|つつ}む→包む：01226_tsutsumu⟧: to put money in a condolence envelope
- {不祝儀袋|ふしゅうぎぶくろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{書|か}き{方|かた}→書き方：13054_kakikata⟧: how to fill out a condolence envelope

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{香典|こうでん}{袋|ぶくろ}→香典袋：24487_koudenbukuro⟧: incense-money envelope — a near synonym, specifically for Buddhist funerals
- ⟦{祝儀袋|しゅうぎぶくろ}→祝儀袋：20945_shuugibukuro⟧: celebratory gift envelope — the opposite, used for weddings and happy occasions

CULTURAL NOTE:
The color and style of the ⟦{水引|みずひき}→水引：29258_mizuhiki⟧ (decorative cords) signal the occasion, so using the wrong envelope is a notable breach of etiquette.
